HEADLINE, and it is not in any changelog: SDK 0.3.265 FLIPPED the systemPromptSnapshot default from off-when-you-pass-append to on-always, so the appended system prompt is recorded on the first request and replayed verbatim on every later request and resume. Satr's append carries the model name itself (envbrief -> runtimeenv.environmentLine), plus project memory and the skill catalog, and agent.js passes resume + model - so a mid-session model switch would silently keep serving the old environment line. Satr sits on 0.3.261 so it is NOT affected today: this is a GATE ON THE UPGRADE, not a bug to fix now. Measured by diffing sdk.d.ts across four packages, not read from an announcement.

That gives an exact, version-to-version contract diff of a wrapped engine that publishes no release notes, with no API key and no login. evaluated_2026_09_12: npm update --package-lock-only run on a COPY of package.json + package-lock.json in a temp directory, then npm audit re-run on the result -> NOT a dependency, a measurement TECHNIQUE worth reusing: it prices a lockfile-only security fix exactly, distinguishes a name-scoped update from an unscoped one, and proves package.json is untouched - all without installing anything or touching the repo. Three runs this edition: `npm install --package-lock-only` (changes nothing - it preserves existing resolutions), unscoped `npm update` (23->14 but crosses the agent-sdk gate), and scoped `npm update <five names>` (23->18, runtime-vulnerable 7->2, agent-sdk unmoved). Limit: it measures version RESOLUTION, not a successful npm ci or test suite.

Classifying npm audit findings by matching each affected package's own PATH and dev flag in package-lock.json against the advisory's affected RANGE - rather than reading the totals or the package name - is what exposed the five-edition misclassification. A package can appear both dev and runtime at different paths with different versions (builder-util-runtime: 9.2.10 dev and vulnerable, 9.7.0 runtime and fixed).
